deadline.value: International application deadline for Fall 2027 entry is March 15, 2027 (Spring is October 1); the general/domestic Fall deadline is April 15, 2027.
deadline.quote: Application Deadlines: Fall – April 15 | Spring – November 1 | International Application Deadlines: Fall – March 15 | Spring – October 1

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for Chemistry (discontinued by ETS in May 2023; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Students enter the program working with the Graduate Program Director and formulate their plan of study and research before selecting a Dissertation Advisor.
supervisor.quote: Students entering the program must formulate a course of study and research in consultation with the Graduate Program Director (or with the student’s Dissertation Advisor once an Advisor has been chosen).

funding.value: Funding availability or assistantship guarantees for Applied Chemistry PhD students are not stated on the department page or in the Graduate Catalog; consult the program directly (DSU financial aid notes federal/institutional aid via FAFSA is limited to US citizens/eligible non-citizens, while departmental grant fellowships and assistantships vary by program).

entry_route.value: Applicants must have earned (or be completing) a bachelor's degree in Chemistry or a closely related field with a minimum 3.0 GPA in the major and at least 20 undergraduate chemistry credits.
entry_route.quote: For admission to this program, applicants must show evidence that they have earned (or will earn at the end of the semester before admission into the Graduate Program) the bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, or a closely related field, at an accredited college or university and possess the ability to carry out graduate work of high quality.

notes: Requires 60 total credits (18 dissertation credits), 20 undergraduate chemistry credits (8 organic, 4 physical, 4 analytical, 4 inorganic), two recommendation letters, and a 1-2 page interest statement.
name: Ph.D. in Applied Chemistry
